title: "Part 2 – R and the IDE"

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/housing-one-day-data-tools.html#/part-2-r-and-the-ide){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 2 introduces the case, because every line of R that you write today works on its data, then the place where R is written and R itself, from assigning a value to drawing a plot. The last half hour is yours.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the paper | The paper of the original authors (OAs): the question that it asks, the design, the email word for word, what came back for each of the six names, the four outcomes that were coded, and the claim as SCORE selected it. | 16 minutes |
| Slides, the IDE, with [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd) as the follow-up | The four places of an IDE that are worth knowing, why you open the folder of the workspace rather than a single file, and the different jobs of the console and the script. With the workspace, follow along in your IDE. | 10 minutes |
| Slides, the R tutorial, with [Getting started with R](../../companion/intro-r.qmd) as the follow-up | R in one slide, reading and inspecting the data, the verbs of datawizard that work on rows and columns, tables and tests, model formulas, a plot with tinyplot, causal graphs in R, and the error messages that you are most likely to meet. Type along in any cell of the browser lab, or in the console of your IDE. | 30 minutes |
| [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-2-data) Task 2, or your report or `working_script.R` | Count the emails, the bounced ones, the delivered ones, the replies and the replies with a greeting code; count the same for each group of names, with the share of the coded replies that greeted the sender by name; draw that share for each of the six names; then change one thing, such as counting by `name_sex` in place of `group`, and read what changes. | 34 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you can find your way around an IDE, read and write the R of the tutorial, and you have counted and drawn what came back for each of the six names: 1,014 emails, 23 bounced, 991 delivered, 563 replies and 558 replies with a greeting code.
